tagline: Leading media and entertainment company across political news, business finance, golf and sports
hero_kpi_rationale: Primary performance indicator for a media and entertainment company operating in four key markets (political news, personal finance, golf, and sports). Revenue reflects the company's ability to monetize its portfolio of complementary brands and digital platforms.

kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to Versant shareholders
kpis.description: Net income attributable to Versant, down 31.8% year-over-year, impacted by higher operating costs following the separation from Comcast

kpis.name: Advertising Revenue

kpis.name: Revenue

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA down 14.5%, reflecting operational challenges and higher structural costs

kpis.name: Linear Distribution Subscriber Decline
kpis.explanation: Ongoing decline in traditional MVPD subscriber base affecting linear distribution revenue
kpis.description: The linear distribution segment, representing 61% of total revenue, declined 5.4% in 2025 and 6.6% in 2024, reflecting shifting consumer preferences toward streaming and digital platforms
kpis.signal: Ongoing decline in the linear segment

risks.title: Decline in traditional video service subscribers
risks.score_rationale: Linear distribution represents 61% of total revenue and declined 5.4% in 2025 and 6.6% in 2024. The ongoing decline in traditional MVPD subscribers directly impacts distribution revenue and is expected to continue long-term.

risks.title: Decline in advertising revenue
risks.score_rationale: Advertising revenue declined 8.9% in 2025, affected by increased competition, audience fragmentation, and rising competition for consumer leisure time.

risks.title: Increased competition in the content market
risks.score_rationale: The programming market, particularly sports rights, has become significantly more competitive and expensive. The company must allocate substantial resources to acquire compelling content to remain competitive.

risks.title: Increased structural costs related to the separation
risks.score_rationale: Following the separation from Comcast, the company incurred approximately $3 billion in debt and must bear additional public company costs (external reporting, internal audit, treasury, investor relations, board of directors).

risks.title: Dependence on advertising and macroeconomic fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: A substantial portion of revenue (24% from advertising) depends on advertising, which is affected by macroeconomic conditions, election cycles, and the timing of major sporting events.

risks.title: Regulatory and compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to government and industry regulations as a standalone public company, including SEC and Nasdaq requirements, which could impact its operations.

risks.title: Reputation and brand positioning risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is establishing its brand as a standalone public entity. Increased public scrutiny, geopolitical tensions, and rapid consumer reactions have heightened reputation concerns.

risks.title: Concentration of control shareholders
risks.score_rationale: Comcast Corporation holds 85.7% of voting power through Class B shares with ten votes per share, creating a significant concentration of control and limiting the influence of other shareholders.
